note: Contract §139.8 (docs/specs/npc-acts-first.md D9): the Keeper's stakes die for a person who has no prepared reaction this turn. It is the table's die, not the CoC 7e Luck roll: Luck is the player's, per investigator, spent and recovered; this die is the Keeper's, per situation. Once per person per turn, before the table generates what that person does, the kernel takes a base rung (base_by_disposition over the person's combat disposition, else base_by_archetype over the rulebook archetype the table pinned for them, else default_rung), moves it by the step of every shift whose condition holds, clamps it to the first and last rung, and rolls 1d100: at most severe_at_most is `severe`, else at most escalates_at_most is `escalates`, else `nothing`. Rungs are listed from the least dangerous to the most, and neither number falls from one rung to the next. No rung makes `severe` certain. The line of the rung and outcome is what the generator is told: a degree, never an action. Every number lives here; the kernel writes no threshold of its own. Shift conditions: attacked_this_turn (this turn an attack roll was made against the person, or they lost hit points), hp_at_most_half (hit points at most hp_fraction_at_most of their maximum), table_clock_past_half (a threat clock of this table stands above clock_fraction_above of its segments), stance_friendly (the person's stance word from the ledger, §17.3, is one of stance_in). A shift absent from this table moves nothing.
